reason: The quotes and line numbers are accurate: SetupWizard.java:1945 and 2016 drop the boolean returned by AdminDeployManager.removeSpawnPoint/removeMobSpawnPoint (AdminDeployManager.java:656-661 and 692-697 return false exactly when the index is out of range), the "spawn point #N removed" message at 1950-1951 / 2020-2021 fires unconditionally, and autoSave(player) at 1953 / 2023 sits in the same unconditional branch, while the villager branch at 1860 does check its boolean. A stale tag is demonstrably reachable: nothing closes or rebuilds an open wizard view on external changes (SetupWizard has only two @EventHandler methods, onInventoryClick:1734 and onQuit:2180, so no InventoryCloseEvent listener), the GUI is a plain Bukkit.createInventory whose items carry absolute indices (refreshSpawnGui:463 "setup-spawn-" + i), and /hilltop deploy clearspawns -> confirmclear (HilltopCommandHandler.java:1000-1016, confirmClear:789-825) clears the shared AdminDeployManager list without touching the viewer's inventory. However the stated impact is inverted: removeSpawnPoint can only return false when 0 <= index < size fails, i.e. when no point exists at that index, so the clicked point can never be "still deployed" nor "reappear" - refreshSpawnGui at 1952 immediately rebuilds from the live (already empty/shorter) list and the stale entry vanishes. autoSave on that path cannot resurrect data either (removeSpawnPoint only calls saveSpawnPoints on success, and deployment-context managers re-read arenas.yml on every deploy() call at SetupWizard.java:133), so the actual harm is a misleading "#N removed" line plus a redundant save/"saved" confirmation for an entry that was already gone. The genuinely dangerous stale-index case - a partial shrink that shifts indices so a click deletes a different point - takes the true-return branch and is not caused by the discarded boolean, so the medium severity is not supported.
